To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Personality depends on the medium, with differences arising from the affordances of the medium.
personality traits are different on Facebook, Snapchat, and offline.

(1) people self-report different personalities in social media than in real life; (2) the differences between offline and social media are not uniform but depend on the social media affordances and (3) people self-report more Extraversion and Openness in social media that is more transient (Snapchat) than in more permanent social media (Facebook)
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between personality and social media use.
the question of how personality differences in social media arise.
how people perceive their own personality on different media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the medium is the message.
people tend to be less Neurotic, less Open, and less Agreeable on Facebook than in offline settings.
personality is a social construct, and the social context (i.e. the medium) is the most important factor to consider when assessing someone’s personality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people are less Neurotics and less Open on Facebook than in offline life, but more Open on Snapchat.
personality traits are not fixed, but rather they can be changed by the environment in which they are measured.
personality is not a stable construct and is dependent on the medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
personality traits are not stable across different social media platforms.
people are not always who they say they are on social media.
personality is not fixed but depends on the medium.
